novelty: Test whether one causally transferable state carries the bidirectional period-versus-question-mark decision across reporting-frame and direct-question constructions, while leaving reporter rewrites invariant and not transferring an explicit punctuation-copy task. This challenges a head-identity reading of the old question circuit; it does not claim a new circuit merely by rediscovering attention layer 10 or head 10.5.

Test whether one site carries which explicitly introduced person performed an action, expressed as the correct he-versus-she continuation, across independently worded active-voice and passive-voice constructions. The linked location rewrite must remain invariant, and the same site must not transfer an unrelated explicit pronoun-copy task with identical output tokens. This extends pronoun-class and gender-readout evidence to natural, answer-changing antecedent counterfactuals; rediscovering head 12.4 or MLP17 without A1/A2 transfer and control selectivity is not novel.

Test whether a full residual-site donor-to-recipient replacement transfers pending-quote state across both a simple quoted noun phrase and a construction containing an earlier balanced quote pair. The same site must preserve the answer under writer rewrites and must not transfer a natural sentence-end-versus-inch-mark completion with the identical period and quote-token endpoints. This is not a new closer-head discovery and does not revive the invalid legacy quote DAS result.

Replace the abandoned learned-coordinate localization compiler with direct donor interchange of the exact full residual or module-output state at the final prediction position across two syntactic constructions. The screen asks whether one common site transfers both prepositional-phrase and relative-clause subject number while remaining small for noun-identity and attractor-number controls. The reusable scorer now derives C from the frozen task declaration: because Task 14 C preserves the answer, it measures absolute patched-versus-native movement normalized by the median A1/A2 donor effect, under the existing C ceiling. This preserves Task 14 semantics and adds a reusable causal localization step. Finding only that the state is distributed or robust would reproduce sections 1550-1552 and is not novel; novelty would require selective cross-syntax interchange at a specific boundary or a well-supported null under this stronger counterfactual.

The v1 screen never tested its hypothesis: it stopped at the native-capability gate because its control asked the model to follow an instruction ('Copy the visible mark ? after ...'), which GPT-2 small cannot do, so the control scored correct exactly when the shown mark was the period it defaults to. This candidate holds A1, A2 and P byte-identical to the v1 authority and replaces ONLY the control with subject-verb number agreement, which is carried by context rather than instruction and whose native capability already passes in the ledger. It therefore asks v1's unanswered question -- whether one site carries the period-versus-question-mark decision across both constructions while sparing an unrelated behaviour -- rather than a new one.

Holds A1/A2/P byte-identical to the v1 sentence-terminal authority and installs a same-answer control whose base and donor differ in place, subject and reporter. This asks whether the C clause can fail at all in the configuration that underwrites every selective_causal_site verdict on disk: resid:18 demonstrably carries the whole prediction, so a control that stays near zero there is near-unfalsifiable, while a control that rises there and not at specific sites is discriminating. No prior screen varies the control's answer-changing status while holding the target families fixed.

Holds A1/A2/P byte-identical to the v1 quote-parity authority and replaces only the control, which the model cannot perform, with a same-answer control whose base and donor differ in content. This asks v1's unanswered question -- whether one site carries the pending-close state across both constructions while sparing an answer-preserving edit -- for a behaviour that has never been screened at all. The C clause is known not to be at risk in this configuration, so the result is reported as target recovery plus P invariance, with C/A1 at the selected site given as the discriminating statistic rather than the pass itself.

First screen of a temporal-frame variable in this corpus; the prior-art search over circuits/task_*.json returns 0 prior events and 0 already-failed targets for tense, past, present, narrative, was and is, and none of the eight behaviours in the ledger (bracket_pending_opener, numbered_list, numeric_sequence, pronoun_antecedent, quote_parity, sentence_terminal, subject_verb, task14) carries one. subject_verb.number_agreement also predicts a copula, but its variable is the SUBJECT'S NUMBER; the two share an answer position and nothing else. Recipient and donor differ only in an early tense cue and end on the same final token, so a site that transfers the was/is decision is carrying narrative tense rather than any surface property of the final position, and A2 re-expresses the same variable in a relative-clause construction so a single-construction lexical cue cannot satisfy both. The control is same-answer, whose measured ceiling is 0.071 against a 0.35 bar, so the C clause is reported as a statistic and not as a passed test.

Tenth behaviour and the first CONSTRUCTION-OBLIGATORY variable in the corpus: having opened 'either', the model is grammatically committed to 'or', and having opened 'neither', to 'nor'. The prior-art search over circuits/task_*.json returns 0 prior events for correlative, either, neither, disjunction and conjunction, and none of the nine behaviours in the ledger carries a paired connective. This differs from every existing behaviour in what the state IS: bracket_pending_opener and quote_parity track an unclosed delimiter, subject_verb and narrative_tense track a feature of an earlier phrase, and the list behaviours track a value. Here the cue creates a syntactic obligation whose satisfaction is the prediction. Recipient and donor differ only in the correlative word and end on the same final token, and A2 re-expresses the variable in a verb-object construction, so a single-construction cue cannot satisfy both. The control is same-answer with a proven-capable frame; its measured ceiling is 0.034-0.142 against a 0.35 bar, so the C clause is reported as a statistic and not as a passed test.

Extends narrative_tense by varying ONE thing: the distance between the tense cue and the patched final position. A1, A2 and P lose the long shared tail so the cue sits two to four tokens before the prediction; the control is held BYTE-IDENTICAL to v2. The instrument patches only the final input token, so a head that writes the state at an EARLIER position and lets it flow forward is invisible to it. If the resid-only profile is a fact about these behaviours, the short-cue screen should still pass only residual sites. If it is a property of the design, attention sites should now pass, because the state has to be read at or near the patched position.

Eleventh behaviour. The prior-art search over circuits/task_*.json returns 0 prior events for comparative, equative, degree, than and as. The nearest existing behaviour is correlative_state.either_vs_neither, which is also construction-obligatory, but its variable is a COORDINATION choice fixed by a paired connective, while this one is a DEGREE head: 'more' obliges 'than' and 'as' obliges 'as', and the two differ in what licenses the second element. Recipient and donor differ only in the degree word and end on the same adjective token, and A2 re-expresses the variable in a seem-predicate construction so a single-construction cue cannot satisfy both. The control is same-answer and drawn from a different licenser -- 'rather than', a preference construction that also obliges 'than' but carries no degree comparison -- so C and P are not the same edit. Its ceiling in this configuration is 0.034 to 0.142 against a 0.35 bar, so the C clause is a statistic, not a passed test.

Twelfth behaviour. Prior-art search over circuits/task_*.json returns 0 events for complementizer, whether and that. Unlike correlative_state and degree_frame, whose second element is fixed by a FUNCTION word (a paired connective, a degree head), here the licenser is the LEXICAL VERB's subcategorization: 'wondered' selects an interrogative complement and 'remarked' a declarative one. Recipient and donor differ only in that verb and end on the same adverb token, so a transferring site carries the selected complement type rather than a surface property of the final position. A2 re-expresses it in a report-framed construction. The control is same-answer under a third verb that also selects 'that', so C tests a different lexical licenser rather than repeating P.

Thirteenth behaviour. Prior-art search returns 0 events for polarity, negation, any and some. This is the corpus's first LICENSING relation as opposed to an obligation: 'not' does not force ' any' the way 'more' forces ' than', it makes it available, and the positive counterpart 'still' leaves ' some' as the natural continuation. Recipient and donor are a minimal pair differing in exactly one word (not versus still) and ending on the same verb token. A2 re-expresses the variable in a perfect construction. The control is same-answer under two verbs that both take ' some' with no polarity item involved.

Fourteenth behaviour, and it is chosen to TEST A REGISTERED PREDICTION rather than only to add breadth. Across thirteen behaviours the same-answer control statistic C/A1 at the selected site has ordered by dependency TYPE, not by screen: obligations cluster at 0.034-0.080 (bracket, verb_complementizer, sentence_terminal, correlative, degree, quote_parity), narrative_tense sits at 0.142, and the single licensing behaviour (polarity_state) is highest at 0.173. That ordering rests on one licensing screen and could be a property of that stimulus set. This is a SECOND licensing behaviour, with a different licenser: subject-auxiliary inversion rather than negation. Prior-art search returns 0 events for interrogative, question, inversion, licensing and npi. Recipient and donor differ only in word order and end on the same verb token; A2 re-expresses it in a perfect construction.
